acceptance_condition: An answer giving: core definitions and guarantees from each paper; an explicit statement of what each framework abstracts away (truth, evidence quality, influence); and at least one observation per paper about a condition under which conflict-free merging or admissible-set reasoning preserves vs destroys information; with PDF page markers.
rationale: The note's synthesis/adjudication stage and its aggregation-only baseline need formal grounding: argumentation semantics can model structured Q/A conflict resolution, and CRDT results characterize when order-free aggregation loses nothing — together they bound what communication can add over merge-based aggregation.
text: What formal machinery do Dung 1995 (papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt) and Shapiro et al. 2011 (papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt) provide that is relevant to agent communication design: for Dung, the definitions of argumentation frameworks, attack relations, admissible/preferred/stable/grounded extensions and what they guarantee about justified conclusions; for Shapiro, the definitions of CRDTs, strong eventual consistency, commutativity/idempotence and what they guarantee about merging concurrent updates without coordination. Note what each framework does NOT model (e.g., evidential weight, truth) since that limits their direct application. Record key definitions with `===== PDF PAGE N =====` markers.
